about: Workshop lessons for the card catalog. Every visitor sees these. Newest entries go at the end; the page shows the newest first.

lessons.title: Projects: a workbench that remembers
lessons.body: A project is its own workspace in Claude, with its own chats and its own shelf of knowledge. You can upload documents, text, code or other files to that shelf, and Claude uses them as background for every chat in the project. You can also write project instructions, like asking for a friendlier tone or a particular point of view, so you don't have to repeat yourself each time. Everyone can make projects, even on a free account, which allows up to five.
lessons.tryIt: Make a project called Homework Helper, upload this week's reading, and add one instruction: explain things step by step and ask me a question back.

lessons.title: Artifacts: things you'd put in front of someone
lessons.body: Anthropic describes an artifact as anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a document, a slide deck, a design, a dashboard or a small interactive tool. It opens beside your chat, where you can keep changing it by asking Claude, or edit some kinds directly, like typing in a doc. Everything you make is saved in the Artifacts tab in your sidebar, and it starts out private to you until you share it.
lessons.tryIt: Ask Claude: make a one-page poster for our family game night, with the date, the snacks and the rules for choosing a game.

source.title: What are artifacts and how do I use them? (Claude Help Center)

lessons.title: CLAUDE.md: the shop rules Claude reads first
lessons.body: Each Claude Code session starts fresh, so a CLAUDE.md file is how you hand Claude the standing rules for a project. It is a plain Markdown file in the project folder that Claude reads at the start of every session. Typing /init asks Claude to look at your code and write a starter file for you, and /memory shows which files are loaded. Keep it short, under about 200 lines, and specific: 'Run npm test before committing' works much better than 'test your changes'.
lessons.tryIt: Open a project in Claude Code, type /init, then read the file it writes and cross out anything that isn't really a rule.

source.title: How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code Docs)

lessons.title: Connectors: plugging Claude into your apps
lessons.body: A connector lets Claude reach one of your other apps, like Google Drive, Slack or Linear, so it can find your information there and even take actions, such as creating a task. You add one under Customize, then Connectors, pick the app and sign in. In a chat, the + button lets you switch on just the connectors you want for that conversation. Claude only sees what your own account can see in that app, so only connect services you trust and actually need.
lessons.tryIt: Connect Google Drive, switch it on in a new chat, and ask Claude to find last month's shared family document and sum it up in three bullet points.

source.title: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities (Claude Help Center)

lessons.title: When Claude sounds sure but is wrong
lessons.body: Claude can sometimes write things that look correct but are mistaken. Anthropic calls this hallucinating, and it happens because of limits in today's AI models. Claude might not know the latest news, and it can even produce quotes that sound convincing but aren't real. So don't treat Claude as your only source of truth, especially for important decisions. When Claude searches the web, open the sources it cites, because the original page may hold details Claude left out. If an answer is wrong or unhelpful, tap the thumbs-down button to tell Anthropic.
lessons.tryIt: Ask Claude a question about something you know well, like your hometown's history, then check one of its claims against a source you trust.

source.title: Claude is providing incorrect or misleading responses (Claude Help Center)

lessons.title: Hand Claude your files
lessons.body: You can give Claude a file to read instead of pasting text. Click the + button in the chat box and choose Add files or photos, or just drag a file into the chat. Claude reads PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, plain text and photos. For PDFs up to 100 pages it can also read the charts and pictures inside; for other documents it reads the text only. Files added to a project's Files section stay there for every chat in that project, so you don't have to upload them again.
lessons.tryIt: Upload a recent utility bill or receipt as a PDF and ask Claude: what are the three most important numbers on this, and is anything unusual?

source.title: Upload files to Claude (Claude Help Center)
